Thanks Anika — attaching a short 'commencement checklist' below that maps to our gate categories (network, identity, kms, routing, monitoring). This is intentionally minimal so your team can triage quickly during the maintenance window.

--- Commencement checklist (Redwood ingress) ---
1) VPC peering / interconnect: BGP session established, relevant CIDR routes present, egress filtering verified.
2) Service account mapping: service accounts for inference runtime created, IAM roles assigned, key rotation policy documented.
3) KMS access: test decrypt/encrypt from a bastion host, ensure HSM key policy allows Redwood service principal.
4) DNS & routing: internal DNS entries created for model endpoints + healthcheck path; NAT/egress rules permit telemetry to our observability endpoints.
5) Firewall rules & SGs: only required ports (443, 10250 for kube metrics) open; deny all else.
6) Audit & logs: CloudTrail/Flow logs enabled, retention policy matching contract (min 90 days), log forwarding endpoint reachable.
7) Canary deployment plan: a small model shard routed to canary pool; auto-fallback policy configured.
8) Rollback trigger: documented playbook + contact list for immediate rollback.

I'll join the window to validate test decrypt and a short end-to-end inference call.

-priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Couple of clarifications from our side:
- On the KMS policy: we need a key-grant entry for 'redwood-inference@redwood-system', scope: Encrypt/Decrypt and GenerateDataKey. Please confirm principal format for your KMS.
- Network MTU: if you're using jumbo frames (>1500), note our recommended MTU is 9000 for the GPU farm to reduce fragmentation.
- Healthcheck URL: /_healthz returns 200 within 3s; if your LB rewrites host headers let us know.

Also adding a short attachment: minimal test vectors (text prompts) we'll use for quality smoke.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
